read_battery: Read the phone battery percentage, charge level, and current battery status. Use this when the user asks how much battery the phone has or what the battery percentage is.
set_volume: Set the phone media volume percentage from 0 to 100.
media_control: Control media playback on the phone: play, pause, toggle play/pause, or skip to the next or previous track.
open_website: Open a website URL in the phone browser.
open_settings: Open an Android system settings screen.
navigate: Show map directions to a destination address or place name.
browse_open: Open a URL in Jarvis's internal browser. The page can then be read, clicked, and filled with the other browse tools.
browse_read: Read the current internal-browser page: title, text, links, and form fields with IDs and a page token. Call this after browse_open and before browse_click, browse_fill, browse_submit, or browse_login; IDs and tokens expire when the page changes.
browse_click: Click a link or button from the latest browse_read result. The link ID and page token must come from that read; stale targets are rejected and never followed.
browse_back: Go back one page in the internal browser history.
browse_forward: Go forward one page in the internal browser history.
browse_fill: Fill a form field from the latest browse_read result. The field ID and page token must come from that read; stale targets are rejected. Filling alone never submits the form.
browse_submit: Submit the filled form on the current internal-browser page. The page token must come from the latest browse_read. Submissions need the user's approval bound to the final destination and form content; without it this reports what would be submitted and asks for approval instead of sending anything.
browse_handoff: Open the current internal-browser page in the phone's own browser app.
browse_login: Fill the current page's login form with the password manager. Credentials are never shown to the model or written anywhere; only the outcome is reported. The page token must come from the latest browse_read.
screen_observe: Look at the current phone screen and return a compact list of the visible interactive elements with IDs and an observation token. Call this before screen_tap, screen_scroll, or screen_type; element IDs and tokens expire when the screen changes.
screen_tap: Tap a screen element from the latest screen_observe result. The target ID and token must come from that observation; stale or mismatched targets are rejected and never tapped.
screen_scroll: Scroll a scrollable element from the latest screen_observe result up or down. The target ID and token must come from that observation; stale targets are rejected.
screen_type: Type text into an editable field from the latest screen_observe result. The target ID and token must come from that observation; stale targets are rejected.
create_reminder: Schedule a one-shot reminder that alerts the user at the requested time with the given message. Use when the user asks to be reminded of something at a specific time. The reminder is written to the workflow ledger and fires an Android alarm; the reply confirms only what was actually scheduled.
show_schedule: List the user's scheduled reminders and upcoming routine runs, or report honestly that nothing is scheduled. Use when the user asks what is scheduled or where a reminder went.
post_notification: Post a notification to the user with a title and text. Use when the user asks to post, send, or show a notification.
